unlisted_practices: Regulators should consider the healthcare relationship, patient autonomy, informed consent and shared decision-making, not only risk and efficacy, when assessing clinical decision support software.
Build mechanisms for practitioner responsibility, shared decision-making, and patient autonomy and consent into AI product design beyond caveats that the final decision rests with the practitioner.
Consider adopting dynamic consent mechanisms for AI-supported care.
Consider whether product-based regulatory evaluation modeled on medical devices and pharmaceuticals is appropriate for clinical decision support software.
Extend regulatory attention to unregulated AI such as large language models used in healthcare.

screen.reason: The paper presents a conceptual framework and ethical/regulatory textual analysis regarding relational ethics and governance of AI in healthcare, functioning as commentary/governance recommendations rather than an empirical evaluation of an AI tool.
